name: read-aloud
description: Read Markdown, text, code and PDF files aloud in a natural neural voice (Kokoro). Free, open source, and fully offline after a one-time model download.

enumDescriptions: Kokoro neural voice (natural, offline after a one-time model download).
Operating-system voice: 'say' on macOS, System.Speech on Windows, espeak-ng on Linux. No download, lower quality.
Piper neural voice via a locally installed 'piper' executable and a voice model you provide.

readAloud.fallbackToNative.description: If the selected neural provider fails to start (for example the model cannot be downloaded), fall back to the operating-system voice.

readAloud.playbackRate.description: Initial playback speed multiplier. Changed live with the Faster / Slower commands and the player slider.

readAloud.prefetchSentences.description: Upper limit on sentences synthesized ahead of playback. The buffer normally fills by time (readAloud.bufferSeconds).

enumDescriptions: Play inside the Read Aloud panel: gapless and instant pause/speed, but VS Code requires one click or key press in the panel each time it is opened.

Play through the operating system (PowerShell SoundPlayer on Windows, afplay on macOS, paplay/aplay/ffplay on Linux): no click needed. Pause restarts the current sentence and speed changes apply to upcoming sentences.

readAloud.systemAudio.command.description: Optional custom player for system output, e.g. "mpv --no-video {file}". Empty picks the platform default.

readAloud.bufferSeconds.description: Seconds of speech to keep synthesized ahead of playback. Raise it on slow computers to reduce pauses (uses more memory and CPU up front).

readAloud.stopOnEditorChange.description: Stop reading when you switch to a different file.

readAloud.maxSentenceLength.description: Very long sentences are split into chunks of about this many characters. Smaller chunks start faster and react faster to Stop and voice changes; larger chunks give slightly smoother prosody.

readAloud.markdown.codeBlocks.description: What to do with fenced code blocks in Markdown: announce ('Code block skipped'), skip silently, or read the code.

readAloud.pdf.announcePages.description: Say the page number when a new PDF page starts.

readAloud.follow.transcriptsDirectory.description: Folder with Claude Code session transcripts. Empty uses ~/.claude/projects.

readAloud.follow.pollIntervalMs.description: How often (ms) the Claude transcript is checked for new replies while following.

readAloud.follow.readSummaries.description: While following Claude, also read the short progress summaries shown between tool calls (the lines marked 'summary' in the chat).

readAloud.follow.announceStart.description: Say a short confirmation when following starts, so you know audio is working.

readAloud.kokoro.voice.description: Kokoro voice. af_/am_ = American English female/male, bf_/bm_ = British English female/male. Use 'Read Aloud: Select Voice' to hear samples. (Only English voices are available: the bundled phonemizer ships English data only.)

readAloud.kokoro.speed.description: Speaking rate used when synthesizing with Kokoro (independent of playback speed).

enumDescriptions: Full precision, best quality (about 325 MB download).
8-bit quantized, slightly lower quality (about 92 MB download).
readAloud.kokoro.model.description: Which Kokoro model file to download and use. Changing this triggers a new download.

readAloud.kokoro.keepAliveMinutes.description: Minutes of inactivity after which the Kokoro helper process is shut down to free about 500 MB of memory. The next read then takes a few seconds to restart it. 0 keeps it running until VS Code closes.

readAloud.kokoro.threads.description: CPU threads for speech synthesis. 0 lets ONNX Runtime decide (usually the number of physical cores). Try the number of performance cores if the benchmark is slow.

readAloud.kokoro.downloadBaseUrl.description: Base URL the Kokoro model and voice files are downloaded from. Point this at a mirror if GitHub is blocked on your network.

readAloud.kokoro.modelDirectory.description: Optional folder containing kokoro-v1.0.onnx / kokoro-v1.0.int8.onnx and voices-v1.0.bin that you downloaded yourself. Leave empty to use the extension's storage folder.

readAloud.native.voice.description: Operating-system voice name (for example 'Samantha' on macOS, 'Microsoft Zira Desktop' on Windows, 'en-us' on espeak-ng). Empty uses the system default.

readAloud.native.wordsPerMinute.description: Speaking rate for the operating-system voice.

readAloud.piper.executable.description: Path to the piper executable (or just 'piper' if it is on your PATH).

readAloud.piper.model.description: Path to a Piper voice model (.onnx). The matching .onnx.json must sit next to it.

readAloud.piper.speaker.description: Speaker id for multi-speaker Piper models.
